summary: infrabench downloads and executes opaque binaries configured as an XMRig-shaped cryptominer
details: The package's only public entry point, `harness.run`, downloads two gzipped native binaries (`inference-core.bin.gz` and `edge-conn.bin.gz`) from a caller-supplied `edge` HTTPS host, chmods them 0755, and spawns them via `subprocess.Popen`. The sha256 values embedded in `ARTIFACTS` are fetched from the same host that serves the bytes, so they establish integrity only, not provenance — whoever operates the `edge` host controls arbitrary native code execution on the installer's machine. The `inference-core` worker is invoked with a configuration whose schema matches XMRig: a `pools` list with `url`/`user`/`pass`/`keepalive`/`tls`, plus `cpu.threads`, `cpu.mem-locked`, `cache-budget`, `log-period`, and `autosave`; the hardcoded `pass: 'vox'` and the supervisor that restarts the worker on exit and POSTs `alive`/`restart`/`done` heartbeats to `https://<edge>/hb` are consistent with a mining supervisor rather than an ML evaluation harness. A synthetic `_Progress` emits fabricated `step/loss/tok/s` log lines, making the running miner resemble ML training in CI output. The second binary, `edge-conn`, is launched with `access tcp --hostname <host> --url...`, which tunnels local TCP traffic to the operator's edge host and bypasses egress controls. `_hb` additionally POSTs the run id and up to 4000 characters of error traceback (which can include local paths and environment detail) to the same operator-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
